nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, the found items are the list obtained from the empty list by applying one round of the item search of $g$ and $D$ as many times as the length of the list of candidate items of $g$ and $D$.
nodes.title: Items found for a grammar and a DFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, the candidate items form the list of the codes $\langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, for every left-hand side $A$ of a production of $g$ (listed once per production) and all states $p$ and $q$ of $D$.
nodes.title: Candidate items for a grammar and a DFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$, a natural number $x$ is a sound item when there are natural numbers $A$, $p$, $q$ and a word $w$ such that $x = \langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, the nonterminal $A$ yields $w$ in the grammar denoted by $g$, and the automaton denoted by $D$, run on $w$ from state $p$, ends in state $q$.
nodes.title: Sound items for a grammar and a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $R$ a list of natural numbers and $q$ one of the states of $D$. Then for every right-hand side $\beta$, every start state of $\beta$ for $q$ given $R$ is one of the states of $D$.
nodes.title: Start states of a right-hand side are states of the DFA

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $R$ a list of natural numbers (the items found so far) and $q \in \mathbb{N}$. The start states of a right-hand side $\beta$, a list of grammar symbols, for $q$ given $R$ are defined by recursion on $\beta$: for the empty right-hand side they are the one-element list $[q]$, and for a symbol $X$ followed by $\beta'$ they are the states of $D$, in order, at which $X$ fits given $R$ and the…
nodes.title: Start states of a right-hand side in a DFA

nodes.summary: For an encoded grammar $g$, an encoded DFA $D$ and a list $R$ of natural numbers (the items found so far), one round produces the list of the codes $\langle A, \langle p, q \rangle \rangle$, where $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ is the natural-number pairing, for every production $A \to \beta$ of $g$, every state $q$ of $D$ and every start state $p$ of $\beta$ for $q$ given $R$.
nodes.title: One round of the item search against a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $D$ be an encoded DFA, $R$ and $S$ lists of natural numbers (the items found so far and the states where the rest of a right-hand side can start), $X$ a grammar symbol and $p \in \mathbb{N}$. The test is true exactly when either $X$ is a terminal $a$ and the step of $D$ from $p$ on $a$ lies in $S$, or $X$ is a nonterminal $B$ and some $k$ in $S$ has $\langle B, \langle p, k \rangle \rangle$ in $R$, where…
nodes.title: Whether a symbol fits at a DFA state

nodes.summary: For every encoded grammar $g$ and every encoded DFA $D$, the intersection-emptiness test of $g$ and $D$ returns true if and only if the intersection of the language of $g$ and the language of $D$ is empty.
nodes.title: Correctness of the intersection-emptiness test

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded grammar with start nonterminal $S$, let $D$ be an encoded DFA with start state $s$, and write $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle$ for the natural-number pairing. The test of $g$ and $D$ is true exactly when there is no accepting state $f$ of $D$ that is also one of the states of $D$ and for which the code $\langle S, \langle s, f \rangle \rangle$ is among the found items of $g$ and $D$.
nodes.title: The intersection-emptiness test for a grammar and a DFA

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar and $D$ an encoded DFA over an alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, and let $\rho$ be an encoded right-hand side whose decoding yields a word $u$ in the grammar that $g$ denotes. If $p$ is one of the states of $D$ and the automaton that $D$ denotes, run on $u$ from state $p$, ends in state $q$, then $p$ is a start state of $\rho$ for $q$ given the items found for $g$ and…
nodes.title: Completeness of the start states in a DFA

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, every encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$ and every encoded DFA $D$ over $T$, the inclusion test on $g$ and $D$ returns true if and only if the language of $g$ is contained in the language of $D$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the inclusion test

nodes.summary: For an encoded context-free grammar $g$ and an encoded DFA $D$ over the same alphabet $T$, where $T$ has decidable equality, the inclusion test on $g$ and $D$ is the Boolean value of the emptiness test on $g$ and the complement of $D$.
nodes.title: The inclusion test for a grammar and a DFA

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(g, D)$, where $g$ is an encoded context-free grammar over $T$ and $D$ is an encoded DFA over $T$, that the intersection of the language of $g$ and the language of $D$ is empty is decidable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Emptiness of the intersection of a context-free and a regular language is decidable

nodes.summary: For every alphabet $T$ with decidable equality and a primitive recursive encoding, the property of a pair $(g, D)$, where $g$ is an encoded context-free grammar over $T$ and $D$ is an encoded DFA over $T$, that the language of $g$ is contained in the language of $D$ is decidable by a multi-stack machine.
nodes.title: Inclusion of a context-free language in a regular language is decidable

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
